_note: Curated course list. Title, URL, hours and last-modified are filled from the Microsoft Learn Catalog API at build time and link-checked nightly; nothing here is typed by hand except the tags and the proof task. Every course is free (cost RM0). HRD Corp claimable status is null (not confirmed) unless a source is given.

courses.proof_task: List your five most frequent tasks. For each, write one line on what an AI tool could do and one line on what you must still check yourself.
Use an AI assistant to draft a decision letter for a synthetic case, then mark every sentence you had to correct and why.
Hand one weekly admin chore to a prebuilt agent and write a half-page note on what it got right, what it missed, and who signs off.
Automate one routine step (for example an acknowledgement email when a new form arrives) and mark the exact point where a human must approve.
Map a synthetic workflow from intake to close, find the slowest step, and propose one change with its expected effect.
Write a one-page redesign of your team's weekly process that says which steps AI drafts and which steps people decide.
Build a small tracker app for a synthetic team with an AI helper and list three checks you ran before trusting it.
Build a simple FAQ agent from public policy text and write the hand-off rule for when it must pass to a person.
Build a one-page dashboard from 200 synthetic records: volume, cycle time and flagged outliers, with one written finding.
Write five SQL queries against a synthetic table that answer five real questions your team asks every month.
Write a short Python script that checks a synthetic CSV for missing fields and duplicates and prints a summary.
Take a synthetic case file and mark which fields are personal data, who may see them, and how long they should be kept.
Write a one-page privacy checklist for a team that starts using AI on customer files.
Write a review checklist for AI-suggested decisions: what to check for errors, bias and missing evidence before you sign.
Score 20 AI answers to synthetic customer questions on accuracy and tone, and report the three most common failure types.
Write a one-page business case for one AI use in your team, with cost, risk and who stays accountable.
Audit one public form or letter your team sends for accessibility and rewrite it in plain language.
Interview two synthetic personas with different needs and redesign one step of a service to work for both.
Set up a shared channel for a synthetic project and write the team's working agreement in under 200 words.
Estimate the paper, travel or energy footprint of one team process and propose one measurable cut.
Pick one community service process and write how AI could help the people it serves, and where it could harm them.
Explain in one page, for a non-technical colleague, how the AI tool that touches your work makes mistakes.
Load a synthetic dataset, build one cleaned table and one chart, and write what the chart does not show.
